key_insight: The authors construct an explicit counterexample showing Carbery’s sharpened triangle inequality (with c = 2) fails for every p > 2, overturning a proposed almost-orthogonality bound in L^p spaces.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether a stronger triangle inequality quantified by interaction coefficients α_{jk} holds in L^p for p ≥ 2; the paper resolves this by showing the proposed inequality is false for all p > 2 and delineates the limits of almost-orthogonality claims.
method: Construct an explicit finite sequence (f_j) in L^p tailored to maximize pairwise interactions and compute norms to exhibit a violation of the proposed bound.
Provide rigorous analytic estimates of the interaction coefficients α_{jk} and asymptotic analysis showing the inequality cannot hold for any p > 2.
Supplement analytic work with computational/experimental exploration (case study with Grok) to guide search for candidate counterexamples and verify numerical behavior.
impact: Alerts analysts and ML researchers that Carbery-style almost-orthogonality bounds with c = 2 cannot be assumed for p > 2, so proofs or algorithms relying on those inequalities must be re-examined or replaced with valid alternatives; improves rigor in using L^p-based norm bounds in ML theory and signal analysis.
visual_elements: Two-panel schematic: left—statement of Carbery’s bound and intuition (almost-orthogonality); right—counterexample snapshot showing explicit functions and violated inequality.
Heatmap or adjacency matrix of α_{jk} values to visualize strong pairwise interactions driving the failure.
Line/ratio plot of ||sum f_j||_p versus the proposed bound across varying p showing divergence when p > 2.
Proof flowchart: construction → norm computations → contradiction → conclusion, with callouts for analytic and computational steps (Grok-assisted search).
paper_title: Almost-Orthogonality in Lp Spaces: A Case Study with Grok
paper_authors: Ziang Chen, Jaume de Dios Pont, Paata Ivanisvili, Jose Madrid, Haozhu Wang
